Diagnosis: In parser.py, the error-recovery branch calls `reader.read_regex(_rest_of_line)`. `_rest_of_line = r"[^
]*(?:|
|
)?"` tries `` before `
`, so on CRLF it consumes only ``, leaving `
` to be swallowed as leading whitespace by the next binding. Result: invalid binding's original.string ends with `` (not full CRLF), and the valid binding starts with a stray `
` and wrong line number.

Change plan: Reorder the alternation to `(?:
|
|)?` (matching `_newline`/`_end_of_line`), so CRLF is consumed as one unit. This yields invalid original.string including the whole CRLF and the next binding starting at line 2 with original.string exactly `GOOD=ok
`. LF and lone-CR behavior unchanged; repeated invalid lines still consume one terminator each. Single-line edit at src/dotenv/parser.py:30; no other files.
